title: Hosted PR #2 run failed on a real-process clock test's join timing; test budget widened
actor: Claude Code agent (architect/QA reviewer role) on Director request, local WSL session

changes.description: Hosted Foundation run 39359423680 on PR #2 (3f134ad) failed on both attempts in the live-matches stage: clock-process.test.mjs 'actual runner continues with zero clients and a fresh process joins a healthy owner without pausing' read 'processing' where it expects 'running'. A timeline replica shows a fresh process joins 0.8 s after p1's turn starts normally and 1.2-1.9 s on one CPU, against p1's 1.8 s budget; a read landing while the owner commits the timeout sees 'processing'. In every case the timeout committed, p2 became active and nothing stuck, so this is test timing, not a D13 defect. The test budget is widened to 4 s with the same assertions; on one CPU the join lands about 1.2 s in.

RUN-20261020-011 repaired clock-process file on one CPU: 14 of 14 passed. RUN-20261020-012 typecheck, lint and full tests at fingerprint 72167125 passed (369 Node, 24 Python, upstream 406/1 skip, 2 injection). RUN-20261020-014 isolated pipeline passed all 14 stages in 534 s with exact timing and the same counts as RUN-20261020-009. RUN-20261020-013 records the two failed hosted attempts from public metadata.
Dated PLAY-04 validation section for the hosted failure, diagnosis and repair; feature evidence re-bound to RUN-20261020-012/014; dated sentence on the audit status lines; backlog link; handoff.
